newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-HEMMINGS PREDICTS 400 METRES HURDLES WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-HEMMINGS PREDICTS 400 METRES HURDLES WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Jamaican Olympic 400 metres hurdles champion Deon Hemmings predicted on Sunday the world record would be broken at the world championships here.
"The world record is most likely to be broken," said Hemmings, referring to American Kim Batten's time of 52.61 seconds set at the 1995 Gothenburg world championships.
"There are two or three athletes capable of running under 52 seconds," said Hemmings, who clocked this year's second best time in 53.18 last month in Oslo.
Batten run the year's fastest race in 52.97 at the U.S. trials in July in Indianapolis.
"I think it (the new record) should be around 51.90," added Hemmings, who became Jamaica's first Olympic women's champion in any event in Atlanta last year.
The women's 400 metres hurdles final is on Friday.
